summary.text: A 28-year-old woman presented to a clinic with intermittent numbness, tingling and weakness in both hands and feet and difficulty lifting the left foot, triggered by increased use of the extremities and relieved by rest, with a prior left wrist carpal tunnel syndrome surgery.

Examination showed 1/5 left ankle and great toe dorsiflexion strength, 5/5 strength elsewhere, a sensory deficit along the lateral left leg, diffusely hyperactive reflexes and an unremarkable cranial nerve examination. EMG showed slowed conduction with conduction blocks, and VEPs showed bilateral P100 prolongation. Brain MRI showed multiple periventricular and juxtacortical T2/FLAIR lesions with one enhancing left centrum semiovale lesion; cervical spine MRI was normal. NMO and MOG antibodies and CSF oligoclonal bands were negative.

The EMG findings were consistent with a sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy; the MRI findings supported radiologically isolated syndrome under the 2023 McDonald criteria. Given a history of recurrent entrapment neuropathies, HNPP was considered and genetic testing identified a heterozygous deletion of the entire PMP22 gene, confirming HNPP. The Figure 1 caption described the MRI findings as possibly consistent with RIS or multiple sclerosis.

Physical therapy was recommended to improve distal weakness and preserve functional mobility, and annual brain MRI follow-up was planned to monitor demyelinating lesion burden. At short-term follow-up she remained clinically stable without new neurological symptoms.
